sources.title: Judge blocks DOJ from threatening election officials over noncitizen voting claims
US judge orders Trump administration to cease threats to prosecute election officials
US judge pushes back on Trump arch ‘national security’ argument

en.title: Judge orders DOJ to stop threatening election officials, rejects arch security claim
en.dek: A federal judge halted DOJ threats against election officials and denied the administration’s national security justification for a planned Washington arch.
facts: Judge Trina Thompson issued a temporary restraining order on Oct 30 blocking DOJ threats to prosecute election officials.
The order was issued in connection with a lawsuit filed by unions representing California election workers.
Judge Tanya Chutkan rejected the Trump administration’s use of national security to justify a 76‑meter arch in Washington.
Chutkan noted that the arch would obscure sight lines between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.
body: Judge Trina Thompson issued a temporary restraining order on Oct 30. The order blocks the Justice Department from threatening state and county officials with criminal prosecution over alleged non‑citizen voting, and it was issued in connection with a lawsuit filed by unions representing California election workers.

Critics, including Democratic and some Republican election officials, described the threats as federal overreach, and some officials said they were preparing for potential federal interference in the midterm elections. The Justice Department had no immediate comment on the ruling.

Judge Tanya Chutkan pushed back on the Trump administration’s claim that a 76‑meter arch in Washington is needed for national security, noting that the arch would obscure sight lines between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery. The lawsuit was brought by Vietnam War veterans seeking to stop construction of the arch.

The arch is one of several Trump projects aimed at reshaping Washington, including a White House ballroom and a renovation of the Reflecting Pool, and a judge investigating the arch case also looked into whether Trump administration lawyers had lied to the court. The judge did not issue a ruling in the arch case yet, stating she would decide expeditiously.
en.context: The ruling comes days before the U.S. midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. The Trump administration has taken an aggressive approach to election oversight, such as pressing states for voter‑registration data. The arch would be a 76‑meter structure modeled after the Arc de Triomphe.
en.imageCaption: The US Justice Department in October threatened to prosecute state and county officials who do not cooperate with the Trump administration’s election-related initiatives
